headline: Two US senators, one Republican and one Democrat, have put forward a bill making the Pentagon's biggest AI suppliers report security problems.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: bipartisan bill on military AI suppliers; still only a proposal.
importance_line: The bill would give the Pentagon more sight of how its AI suppliers protect their models, which matters to national security officials and the public, then to the AI companies concerned, but it is only a proposal and has not been voted on.
summary: DefenseScoop reports that Republican Sen. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand put forward the Insider Threat Reporting and Security Guidance Act of 2026, which would make AI companies with Pentagon deals worth $100 million or more share their security practices and report incidents such as stolen model weights (the files holding an AI model's learned settings) within 72 hours. The companies would also have to certify their reports every 90 days, using the Pentagon's buying power to set safety expectations before Congress passes broader AI rules.
notes: Read from the fulltext file. The article also notes the Pentagon-Anthropic dispute and May 2026 deals with other AI firms as background; not used in the entry.
